definitions.meaning: to recommend a course is to speak in favour of it, to champion it
in Scotland a barrister is called by this title

explanation.surface: Someone suggesting a solicitor from Edinburgh to a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are standard senses: a verb meaning to urge or support, and the Scottish title for a barrister.

parts.note: Dover is a Channel port in Kent, England

explanation.surface: A harbour is the sole provider of seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: DOVER is the English ferry port facing France.
explanation.definitionFit: Dover sole is a prized flatfish, an example of the category.

clue.text: Monsters consequently turning on head of security

indicators.note: turning means the word is spun round and read from the end

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, consequently

indicators.note: head of picks the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Monsters therefore attack the chief of security.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogres are man-eating giants in folk tales, a kind of monster.

parts.note: an ass is a fool, a twerp

explanation.surface: A donkey grazing in a Belgian location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ass' suggests a donkey but means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Antwerp is a major port city in Belgium, so it is an example of a Belgian place.

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The finest section of Japanese writing.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the best of a group, the pick or cream.

definitions.meaning: a prison term for the rest of one's days, the longest a court gives
a written account of someone's days from birth to death

explanation.surface: A lengthy sentence found in a book about someone's career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long sentence' reads as grammar but is a prison term.
explanation.definitionFit: A life sentence is the longest prison term, and a written life is a biography.

parts.note: to fancy something is to like it
Ned is a man's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A smart gentleman was compared to someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy man' reads as a lover; split it into 'fancy' and 'man'.
explanation.definitionFit: To liken is to compare, so likened means compared or portrayed as resembling.

definitions.meaning: a device that moves air to cool you down
a follower or enthusiast of a team

explanation.surface: A more laid-back follower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' looks like a comparative adjective but is a noun, something that cools.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan blows air to cool a room, and a fan is also an enthusiast or supporter.

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word for the clergyman is read from its end

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a clergyman's title

explanation.surface: Someone asserts that a vicar is supporting them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support from the clergyman, but it is the turnaround signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to assert or state firmly, a close synonym of claim.

clue.text: Rational but erroneous description of Henry VIII

definitions.meaning: using reason, able to reflect and reason things out
Henry VIII was famously stout, so calling him a slim monarch would be wrong

explanation.surface: A sensible but mistaken account of the Tudor monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second definition as two words, THIN KING: Henry VIII was notoriously fat.
explanation.definitionFit: A reasoning, rational creature is a thinking one, as in 'a thinking person'.

clue.text: Rare gems scattered in Lakeland village

indicators.note: scattered gems are strewn about out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Precious stones strewn around a village in the Lake District.
explanation.walkthrough: Lakeland is the Lake District in northwest England; GRASMERE is a village there, home to Wordsworth.
explanation.definitionFit: Grasmere is a well-known village in the English Lake District, so it is an example of the category.

indicators.note: holds means the word for nothing contains the other letter within it

explanation.surface: Something empty grasping a clip or clasp.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail is a metal spike hammered in to fix things together, a kind of fastener.

clue.text: Rebel in south demanding immediate action

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
urgent means pressing, requiring action now

explanation.surface: An uprising in the south needs swift response.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurgent is a person rising up against authority, a rebel.

clue.text: State that may be so ideal for sap?

indicators.note: may be hints that these letters could become something else once reshuffled

explanation.surface: A condition that might seem perfect to a gullible dupe.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a whole-clue definition, but 'so ideal for sap' rearranged by 'may be' gives all thirteen letters; 'sap' (a fool) makes the clue a nice semi-&lit.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a condition of happiness built on false hopes, a mental state of deluded contentment.

indicators.note: outside means the word for allowed wraps round the other word

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: A young animal is always permitted to go outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' looks like the animal going outdoors, but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A leveret is a young hare in its first year, a kind of young creature.

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters

parts.note: a dress is a costume, a garment

explanation.surface: A very rude outfit that was corrected.
explanation.definitionFit: To redress a wrong is to remedy it, set it right.

indicators.note: used in says the letters sit inside the words that follow, across the gap

explanation.surface: The kind of fuel that powers old cars and lorries.
explanation.walkthrough: DERV is the British name for diesel fuel for road vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Derv is diesel oil for road vehicles, a type of fuel in British usage.

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played about with, put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Asking whether a Tudor is playing draughts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'checkers' looks like the board game, but it means people who check accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: Auditors examine accounts for accuracy, so they are checkers of the books.

clue.text: Where flounders may be found floundering

definitions.meaning: flounders are flatfish living in the ocean

explanation.surface: The place flatfish live, flapping about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flounders' is the fish, while 'floundering' means bewildered.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means literally out in the ocean and, idiomatically, confused or bewildered.

clue.text: Disappointment, ultimately, that hurts very little

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: ouch is what you cry when something hurts

explanation.surface: A letdown at the end causes just a slight pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A touch means a small amount, a tiny bit, as in 'a touch of salt'.

clue.text: Hypocrite taking pence before he accepts a pay increase

indicators.note: before places the letter for pence ahead of the rest

parts.note: p is the abbreviation for pence in British money

indicators.note: accepts means the pronoun takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a rise is the British word for a pay increase

explanation.surface: A two-faced man pocketing pennies before taking a raise.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a pay increase is a 'rise' rather than a 'raise'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pharisee is used of a self-righteous, sanctimonious person, a hypocrite, from the Gospel portrayals.

clue.text: Dance the foxtrot speedily, just taking seconds

indicators.note: taking seconds means picking the second letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: Performing the foxtrot quickly, in only a few moments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seconds' looks like time, but it means second letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A hop is an informal dance or social dance party.

explanation.surface: Second-hand goods taken advantage of.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both second-hand and taken advantage of, two ordinary senses of the same past participle.

definitions.meaning: to see or catch sight of
a pimple or mark on the skin

explanation.surface: Spotting a flaw on someone's face.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to notice it, and a spot is a pimple or blemish.

indicators.note: silly means daft or disordered, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Mocking a foolish devotee of art.
explanation.definitionFit: An aesthete is someone with a refined appreciation of beauty and the arts.
